meta.title: Love Language Test | Discover Your Love Style - DopaBrain
meta.description: Discover your primary love language with Gary Chapman's 5 Love Languages. Take the 30-question test to understand how you give and receive love.

app.title: 💗 Love Language Test
app.subtitle: How do you express and receive love?

q1: What makes you happiest when your partner does it?
q1a: Saying 'I really appreciate you, I love you'
q1b: Helping with chores when I'm busy
q2: When you're hurt by your partner, what do you need most?
q2a: A sincere verbal apology and comforting words
q2b: Showing remorse by doing something for me
q3: What moves you most on special occasions?
q3a: A heartfelt letter written just for me
q3b: Cooking my favorite meal from scratch
q4: When do you feel most loved by your partner?
q4a: When they say 'You're the most important person in my life'
q4b: When they take care of me when I'm sick
q5: If your partner posts about you on social media?
q5a: I'm moved when it includes loving words about me
q5b: I'm moved when they share our everyday moments together
q6: After an argument, what matters most for making up?
q6a: A direct 'I'm sorry, I was wrong' verbal apology
q6b: Doing something thoughtful instead of just saying sorry
q7: How do you feel your partner cares about you?
q7a: When they say 'I love you' and 'good night' every day
q7b: When they bring small gifts or flowers for no reason
q8: What do you hope for from your partner on your birthday?
q8a: A heartfelt birthday message with meaningful words
q8b: A surprise gift of something I've always wanted
q9: How does your partner show love when they're busy?
q9a: Sending a short encouraging text or calling briefly
q9b: Making sure we have dinner together no matter what
q10: What makes a date most meaningful?
q10b: Full attention with no phone distractions
q11: What action makes you feel loved?
q11a: Being told 'You worked so hard today, I'm proud of you'
q11b: My partner naturally holding my hand while walking
q12: After a hard day, what do you want from your partner?
q12a: Empathetic words like 'That sounds exhausting, you did great'
q12b: A warm, silent hug without any words
q13: What shows you that your partner cares?
q13a: Coming to help me immediately when I'm struggling
q13b: Remembering my preferences and giving a thoughtful gift
q14: What do you value most in a relationship?
q14a: My partner going out of their way to help me
q14b: Surprise gifts and special events planned just for me
q15a: Anticipating my needs before I even ask
q15b: Simply sitting close to me without doing anything
q16: What made you feel most excited early in the relationship?
q16a: When my partner helped or took care of something for me
q16b: When we talked for hours and lost track of time
q17: When do you prefer physical touch over other things?
q17a: I'd rather have my partner help solve a problem
q17b: A reassuring pat on the back or hand-holding when I'm struggling
q18: If you had to choose what matters most in a relationship?
q18a: A partner who supports my daily life through helpful actions
q18b: A partner who hugs me often and is affectionate
q19: Why does a partner's gift feel so meaningful?
q19a: When they secretly remembered something I wanted long ago
q19b: I actually value time spent together more than gifts
q20: Which way of celebrating an anniversary feels happier?
q20a: Receiving a special gift my partner carefully prepared
q20b: Spending a long time just the two of us somewhere special
q21: What would you most like to receive from your partner?
q21a: A gift they prepared by remembering my interests
q22a: When they bring back a souvenir just for me from a trip
q22b: When they naturally hold my hand during a movie
q23: When are you happiest being with your partner?
q23a: Having a long conversation at a café with no phones
q23b: Just leaning against each other or cuddling on the couch
q24: During a tough time, what do you want your partner to do?
q24a: Make time to stay with me for a long while
q24b: Gently rub my back or stroke my hair
q25: How do you feel your partner's support?
q25a: Words like 'I believe in you, you've got this'
q25b: Being present at my side during important moments without words
q26: After work, what do you hope your partner has done?
q26a: Prepared a meal or snack waiting for me
q26b: Hugging me right when I walk through the door
q27: How does your partner make you feel special?
q27a: Praising even small things: 'You're the best at this'
q27b: Surprising me with a small unexpected gift for no reason
q28: Why do you enjoy a shared hobby with your partner?
q28a: The teamwork and helping each other through the process
q28b: Simply sharing the same experience in the same space
q29: What action from your partner excites you most?
q29a: A surprise hug from behind or a kiss on the cheek
q29b: A thoughtful gift chosen perfectly for my taste
q30: If you could only pick one thing most important in love?
q30a: Being told 'I love you' every day

desc.W: Your love language is Words of Affirmation. You feel and express love through words. Sincere compliments, heartfelt gratitude, and verbal declarations of love fill your heart like nothing else. A single meaningful sentence is worth more to you than any gift. You may be especially sensitive to criticism and negative language, and a kind word can give you the strength to get through the day.
desc.A: Your love language is Acts of Service. You feel the deepest love when someone does things for you. Actions speak far louder than words, and when your partner goes out of their way to help you, it says 'I truly love you' more powerfully than anything. The thoughtfulness of someone anticipating your needs before you ask is the ultimate expression of love for you.
desc.G: Your love language is Receiving Gifts. It's not about the price tag—what moves you is the heart and intention behind a gift. When your partner remembers your tastes and surprises you, you feel how truly valued you are. The key is not the material object but the feeling of 'they were thinking of me,' which is the essence of love for you.
desc.T: Your love language is Quality Time. To you, love means having someone's full, undivided attention. Putting down the phone, making eye contact, sharing heartfelt conversations, or taking a walk together—these everyday moments are the highest form of love. When quality time decreases, you may feel unloved, so regular dedicated time together is essential.
desc.P: Your love language is Physical Touch. For you, love is felt through the skin. A hug, holding hands, or a gentle pat on the back gives you a far stronger sense of security and connection than words or gifts ever could. On a tough day, a silent embrace from your partner makes all your worries melt away. Physical distance can feel like emotional distance to you.

advice.W: Tell your partner honestly how much their words of praise and encouragement mean to you. Simple phrases like 'thank you,' 'I love you,' and 'great job' exchanged daily can transform your relationship. If your partner's love language differs, understand that their silence doesn't mean a lack of love. Learning each other's love languages and adapting is what deepens a relationship.
advice.A: Communicate clearly and specifically what kind of help you need—don't expect your partner to guess. When they do help, always express gratitude and let them know how much their actions feel like love to you. Make an effort to express love in your partner's language too, and you'll both be happier.
advice.G: Let your partner know that gifts mean a lot to you—and that an inexpensive, heartfelt gift is just as meaningful as an expensive one. Cultivate the habit of noticing your partner's tastes and interests so you can reciprocate. Surprising each other with small gifts even on ordinary days keeps the relationship vibrant. Sharing wish lists is also a great idea.
advice.T: Communicate to your partner how important undivided quality time is to you. When you're on dates, try setting a rule to minimize phone use and focus on each other. Grand plans aren't necessary—cooking together, going for a walk, or watching the same show is the highest form of love. Create a regular 'date day' to make each other a priority.
advice.P: Talk to your partner about how much physical touch grounds and reassures you, and together find a comfort level that works for both of you. Small everyday touches—holding hands, a pat on the shoulder, a kiss on the cheek—accumulate and deepen intimacy greatly. If your partner is less comfortable with touch, don't push; enjoy discovering what works for both of you. Hugging actually reduces stress hormones and releases oxytocin, making you genuinely feel better.
